report.title: Classical lane: verified m=205, |R|=12 (ratio 0.733412); no modulus beat the record in budget
report.summary: I searched square-free moduli for a residue set with no two elements differing by a nonzero square mod m, treating it as max-independent-set on the circulant Cayley graph Cay(Z_m, QR ∪ -QR). Multi-restart randomized greedy (the strongest heuristic here) reproduces the known optimum at m=205 and a branch-and-bound exact check found nothing larger there. Scans across 50–2000 plus a focused heavy search on all square-free multiples of 5 and of 13/17/29/37/41 up to 3000 produced nothing above 0.733412. I submit a freshly verified m=205, |R|=12 certificate (ties the record) as my best checked object.
report.learned: Greedy reproduces the known optimum (12 at m=205), so it is competitive in this small-independent-set regime; the annealing variant was weaker and underperformed greedy. The quality ratio log|R|/log m is a CRT mediant, so a pure product of coprime atoms lies between the two atoms' ratios — meaning 205's record value comes from a NON-product size-12 set (larger than 2 x the Paley(41) independence number), which is exactly why single primes/clean products don't reach it. Good moduli cluster on 5·(p ≡ 1 mod 4): e.g. m=1105=5·13·17 gives |R|=21 (0.7172) and m=65=5·13 gives |R|=7 (0.7331, just under). Dead end: annealing and straight greedy on larger m found nothing above 0.717; no single modulus up to 3000 in the searched families beat 0.733412. Exact B&B hit its node cap above m≈300, so bigger exact runs need a real MIS/clique solver.
report.next: Build the explicit 205 size-12 set and attempt non-product CRT synergy: lift to m=205·p via CRT plus local repair, aiming for |R| > 12·atom(p). Replace the heuristic with an exact MIS/clique solver (networkx/or-tools or a dedicated clique code in a workspace venv) and run exact on m in 200–600 to check for an off-by-one gain (e.g. confirm max at m=265 is really 12, not 13). Mine the Paley-graph clique literature for primes whose clique/independence number is unusually large vs √p — those are the best atoms to CRT-combine.

detail: m = 205, |R| = 12: exponent ½(1 + log|R|/log m) = 0.73341180 (classical record 0.733412, overall 0.75806770413).

lean.statement: 205 is square-free and no two of the 12 residues differ by a square modulo 205
lean.consequence: The exponent ½(1 + log|R| / log m) then follows from Ruzsa's 1984 construction (not formalized here).
